metadata.file_name: 10. Aydoğan & Tat. (2025). Investigating the Performance of Artificial Neural Networks in Predicting Affective Responses .pdf
metadata.title: Investigating the Performance of Artificial Neural Networks in Predicting Affective Responses
metadata.venue: Journal of Measurement and Evaluation in Education and Psychology

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata for the Lebanese sample (5614 participants initially) and then restricts the analytic dataset to 4631 cases after deleting observations with missing or extreme values to satisfy CFA/ANN assumptions. The manuscript does not report the use of PISA complex survey weights or any replicate-weight procedure, and it does not name any weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or software that would automatically apply them. Because the predictive component is an ANN trained on questionnaire Likert responses, the authors appear to have proceeded without explicit survey-weighted estimation; this means results may not be fully representative of the target population under PISA’s sampling design. No grade/school-type filtering is described beyond the missing/extreme-value deletion, and the ANN inputs are the six remaining Awacom items used to predict two held-out items.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variables are affective/intercultural communicative awareness Likert items (Awacom items ST218Q01HA–ST218Q07HA) rather than PV-based cognitive achievement scores. The study instead predicts item responses directly (scaled to 0–1 and then mapped back to ordinal categories), so PV generation/combining is not part of the analysis pipeline. Missing data handling is reported as listwise deletion (cases with missing and extreme values were deleted), so the missing-data strategy is documented.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 Lebanese sample data. Started with 5614 Lebanese students who participated in PISA 2018, then deleted cases with missing data and extreme values to meet assumptions for CFA (SEM) and ANN modeling; the final analytic sample contained 4631 students. No additional grade, school-type, or subgroup restrictions are described beyond this missing/extreme-value deletion.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Best ANN model (Model1) selected by RMSE closeness across all/train/test: RMSE All=.619, Train=.618, Test=.623. Similarity between predicted vs actual Item3: Match ratio=.63; marginal homogeneity test p>.05; Kappa=.42 (moderate). Construct validity/reliability: for predicted subset RMSEA=.106, CFI=.965, TLI=.948, R-square=.983, Loading=.992, Alpha=.903 (vs actual subset RMSEA=.081, CFI=.972, TLI=.959, R-square=.613, Loading=.783, Alpha=.891).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 (Lebanon) Awacom item the study leveraged Item1, Item2, Item4, Item5, and Item6 responses to predict Item3 responses, finding that predicted and actual Item3 responses overlapped at a moderate level (Kappa=.42; match ratio=.63) while CFA fit indices were only partially weakened. This indicates that ANN-based response prediction within the same affective latent construct can preserve measurement structure and slightly improve reliability, suggesting potential for data augmentation or missing-item recovery in intercultural awareness scales, though the study does not establish causal effects and uses listwise deletion for missing/extreme values.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Best ANN model (ModelB) selected by smallest/closest RMSE across all/train/test: RMSE All=.708, Train=.695, Test=.734. Similarity between predicted vs actual Item7: Match ratio=.58; marginal homogeneity test p>.05; Kappa=.37 (low). Construct validity/reliability: for predicted subset RMSEA=.111, CFI=.963, TLI=.944, R-square=.942, Loading=.970, Alpha=.909 (vs actual subset RMSEA=.081, CFI=.972, TLI=.959, R-square=.489, Loading=.700, Alpha=.891).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 (Lebanon) Awacom item the study leveraged Item1, Item2, Item4, Item5, and Item6 responses to predict Item7 responses, finding that overlap with actual Item7 responses was moderate-to-low (Kappa=.37; match ratio=.58) and that model fit indices were partially weakened but remained strong. This indicates that ANN prediction is less accurate for Item7 specifically (consistent with non-linear sensitivity patterns), yet predicted items can still improve factor loadings/variance explained and reliability, suggesting targeted support for scale scoring where some items are harder to predict.

data.outcome_summary: The study uses PISA 2018 Lebanese student questionnaire data and focuses on the Awacom affective latent trait (intercultural communicative awareness). After deleting cases with missing and extreme values, the authors train feed-forward artificial neural networks to predict two held-out Awacom items (Item3 and Item7) from the other six items, scaling ordinal responses to 0–1 for ANN training and then mapping back to ordinal categories. For Item3, the best model (Model1) achieved RMSE around .619 (all) and produced moderate agreement with actual responses (match ratio .63; Kappa .42), with CFA-based validity/reliability showing improved factor loadings and reliability despite weaker fit indices. For Item7, the best model (ModelB) had RMSE around .708 (all) and lower agreement (match ratio .58; Kappa .37), but predicted subsets still improved variance explained, loadings, and reliability. Limitations include listwise deletion for missing/extreme values, no reported use of PISA sampling/replicate weights, and the fact that predictive overlap does not imply causal relationships.
